messages.subject: multiple cores issue
parts:
We have recently installed rstan on multiple Linux servers.
The code works well, until one sets  options(mc.cores= 3) , or any other number greater than 1.

The problem: none of the subprocesses can find rstan (or colorspace, or gridExtra, or...)

I suspect: the libPath is not being passed.  A consequence of the multi-user setup, on multiple clusters with disjoint disk space,  is that the libPath is set on initiation via the Rprofile.site file.   Below is an example from one of the boxes, the "missing" libraries are all in 1 and 2.   The directory names are quite different on other servers.  (All of our group uses ssh -X or other remote desktop methods to link up to one or more different service clusters).  

> .libPaths()

[3] "/home/biotools/r/R-3.2.3/lib64/R/library"                            

Does anyone have any ideas?  

Terry Therneau
Mayo Clinic
ther...@mayo.edu

On Wednesday, August 17, 2016 at 9:44:27 AM UTC-4, Terry Therneau wrote:

The problem: none of the subprocesses can find rstan (or colorspace, or gridExtra, or...)

I suspect: the libPath is not being passed.

This came up many months ago and I thought I fixed it for good, but apparently not. We currently have a line

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/blob/develop/rstan/rstan/R/stanmodel-class.R#L508

that calls .libPaths() on the child processes to register the directories where Rcpp, rstan, and rstanarm are found by the parent process. Does anything come to mind as to why that would not work in your case? Maybe we need to include ggplot2 and gridExtra in that, but I'm not sure what is trying to pull in colorspace.

Thanks,
Ben

P.S. I think we have a RA and funding lined up to implement some survival models in rstanarm this fall. Let me know if you would like to be kept in the loop on that.

messages.author: 5bee1b7204620326
messages.subject: Re: multiple cores issue
parts:
Ben,
  This is using STAN as installed from CRAN.   The obvious thing for me to do is to toss in a print statement or two, which is of course hard to do with namespaces, square or cube that difficulty as soon as S4 enters the picture.  (Is there an analog to assignInNamespace?)  Perhaps I'll have to download the source, but that may be a few weeks given some deadlines.

   I did execute getMethod("sampling", "stanmodel"), and the line you point to is in the local code, so we don't have a version issue.

   Yes, I would be interested in survival problems.  One reason is an open issue in coxme.  Assume a random intercept per group in a Cox model, and now move towards the limit case of only a few subjects per institution.  (This is common in multi-center trials of uncommon diseases.)  If some of the groups have no deaths, the unconstrained intercept for that group is -infinity.   The overall impact of this is to pull var(intercept) towards too large a value.  If the variance gets too large the Laplace approx begins to fail.  I have one nasty data set that breaks coxme and every other package I know, in that the final variance estimate is silly: it predicts some to be nearly immortal.  (It's a terrible model for said data set, but that won't stop users.)   The obvious solution is a strong prior on the variance, e.g. I find a group intercept of -3 = relative risk of 1/20 very had to swallow, no matter how much that hospital's CEO wants to brag.  This of course fits naturally into the MCMC framework.   This has been a practical problem for UNOS (United Network for Organ Sharing), as they are required by law to publish outcome information from all centers.  Without some shrinkage small centers, e.g., any pediatric transplant program, will see extreme highs and lows in the hazard ratio.  On the other hand they don't want to shrink much, so as to respond quickly to any center with a problem in post-transplant care.  

Terry

messages.subject: Re: multiple cores issue
parts:
Ben, 
  Here is one idea.  Say that someone has multiple R libraries which I'll call 'standard' and "new".  When a new package like rstan is added it is put into 'new' for a time due to caution.  However, many of the things it depends on are already in 'standard'.   Your code would include 'new' in the paths, since it only looks for the main routine and not its dependencies, then fail when the routine actually tried to run.  
  This is exactly the case with rstan at Mayo.  The rstan library is in the first element of .libPaths(), gridExtra for instance is in the second.

Terry

messages.author: 5bee1b7204620326
messages.subject: Re: multiple cores issue
parts:
I downloaded the dev source from github and was able to make it work with a change to the code.  My prior make failed (I think) due to an out-of-sync version of StanHeaders.
Short answer: the .libPaths() environment needs to be preserved, not just the rstan library or its imports.

The dependencies list is deep:
> library(tools)
> temp <- available.packages()
> package_dependencies("rstan", db=temp, recursive=TRUE)

$rstan
 [1] "ggplot2"      "StanHeaders"  "methods"      "stats4"       "inline"      
 [6] "gridExtra"    "Rcpp"         "RcppEigen"    "BH"           "utils"       
[11] "Matrix"       "stats"        "digest"       "grid"         "gtable"      
[16] "MASS"         "plyr"         "reshape2"     "scales"       "grDevices"   
[21] "graphics"     "lattice"      "stringr"      "RColorBrewer" "dichromat"   
[26] "munsell"      "labeling"     "colorspace"   "stringi"      "magrittr"    
[31] "tools"       


Here is the relevant line that needs to be added in the stanmodel-class.R file
    ...
            dependencies <- c("Rcpp", "rstan", "rstanarm")
            .paths <- unique(sapply(dependencies, FUN = function(d) {
                dirname(system.file(package = d))
            }))
            .paths <- .paths[.paths != ""]
            .paths <- unique(c(.paths, .libPaths()))     # add this line
   ...
I will guess that .libPaths() alone isn't enough, e.g., for the user who used library(rstan, lib.loc="my_local_lib").  But the old libPath can't be left out either unless you want to recursively chase down all the dependencies of dependencies.  At our inst  things further down that list are not in the same place as rstan, Rcpp, or rstanarm.    (Over 500 users on multiple shared servers of multiple types -- I'm not going to second guess how or why the sys admins organized things into multiple libraries.  The linux bunch at least are a very bright crew.)

Terry T.

Hi Terry,

When you have a chance, can you try the development version of rstan which has an attempted fix for this issue? Just call

devtools::install_github("stan-dev/rstan", ref = "develop", subdir = "rstan/rstan", dependencies = TRUE)

You can make it install faster if you use multiple cores by calling Sys.setenv(MAKEFLAGS = 8) or something beforehand.

Ben
